items.title: ByteDance and Hollywood reach copyright pact for AI video and image tools
items.summary: ByteDance and the Motion Picture Association (MPA) have reached an agreement to strengthen copyright safeguards for the Chinese tech giant's AI video and image-generation models, marking a notable shift from confrontation toward cooperation over generative AI and intellectual property.

items.title: Humanoid robots expose the limits of chasing higher TOPS
items.summary: Humanoid robots are moving from demonstrations toward mass production, changing the priorities of chip design. Instead of simply chasing higher AI compute and TOPS, or trillions of operations per second, the industry is increasingly focused on how efficiently perception, computing, decision-making, and control can work together within tight power, cost, and latency constraints.

items.title: MediaTek widens ASIC services as market share surges
items.summary: MediaTek has reportedly landed major orders for Google TPU products in recent years, even appearing to challenge Broadcom's position. At a recent earnings call, MediaTek also raised its 2027 ASIC market share target to 15% to 20%, and industry watchers largely credit that goal to the breadth of MediaTek's ASIC services.

items.title: SpaceX, Nvidia push space AI from lunar exploration toward orbital data centers
items.summary: As SpaceX accelerates its push into space-based AI data centers and Nvidia brings Jetson GPUs into lunar exploration missions, the race to build computing infrastructure beyond Earth is moving from proof-of-concept experiments toward actual deployment.

items.title: European industrial suppliers gain from AI data center buildout
items.summary: European makers of vacuum pumps, heat exchangers, and industrial gases are seeing new demand from the rapid buildout of AI factories, according to Bloomberg. The shift is giving investors fresh ways to gain exposure to artificial intelligence through industrial suppliers tied to semiconductor plants and data centers.

items.title: OpenAI revenue chief to exit as company advances IPO preparations
items.summary: OpenAI said its revenue chief, Denise Dresser, will step down after less than a year in the role, adding another senior departure as the artificial intelligence company moves through IPO preparations. She said on LinkedIn that she was honored to support AI development and will stay briefly to help with the transition.

items.title: South Korea telcos pass KRW1 trillion in first-half AI data center revenue
items.summary: South Korea's three major telecom operators generated more than KRW1 trillion (approx. US$706 billion) in combined artificial intelligence data center revenue in the first half of 2026, as demand for AI computing lifted utilization across their facilities. The companies are now expanding capacity in stages, with carriers saying they want to secure customer demand before committing to larger investments.

items.title: High jet fuel costs could squeeze low-cost airlines for months
items.summary: Jet fuel prices may remain elevated for months even if geopolitical tensions ease, the challenge stemming not only from crude supply but also from global refining capacity already operating near full utilization, leaving no room to increase output of refined products.
